previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis on immunosuppressive therapy was admitted for a severe joint pain flare affecting multiple left-sided joints, beginning in the shoulder and spreading overnight. The flare was attributed to recent tapering of prednisone and discontinuation of azathioprine. Evaluation showed no signs of infection in the joints or prior left leg fluid collections, with stable imaging and negative cultures. The patient was treated with an increase in prednisone to 40 mg daily, rotation from hydromorphone to oxycodone for better pain control, and uptitration of gabapentin and lidocaine patches. Pain improved significantly, and the patient remained afebrile and stable. A minor fall during admission prompted a head CT, which showed no acute abnormalities. He was discharged home with optimized pain and arthritis management, instructions to follow up with rheumatology, and guidance on monitoring for infection or worsening symptoms.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o M with refractory psoriatic arthritis on immune 
suppression, multiple recent hospitalizations for evaluation of 
multiple fluid collections in left lower extremity, who returns 
with arthritic pain in left sided joints as well as GI upset.  

# Joint Pains: Patient recently admitted for identical symptoms, 
felt to be consisent with psoriatic arthritis flare. There was 
concern that, given the patient's significant diarrhea, he may 
not be absorbing his PO steroids and pain medications. Per 
rheumatology recs, he was started on methylprednisolone 30mg IV 
BID. He was continued on his azathioprine. He was placed on 
dilaudid IV for pain control. He was continued on his home 
regimen of gabapentin, indomethacin, and MSContin. Over time, 
his pain improved. He was transitioned to a PO prednisone taper 
and placed back on his home PO pain medications. He was 
discharged with instructions to follow-up with his outpatient 
rheumatologist.

# GI complaints: Pt reported that he gets significant diarrhea 
with worsening of his psoriatic arthritis symptoms.  He reported 
that there was some concern that he could have IBD. On 
presentation, the patient complained of significant diarrhea 
over the past few days. However, his diarrhea drastically 
improved on admission. He was instructed to f/u with his outpt 
gastroenterologist after d/c for further work-up of possible 
IBD.

# Diabetes Mellitus type 2: Patient followed at ___ as 
outpatient.  He was continued on his home insulin regimen.

# Hypertension: Continued on hydrochlorothiazide, metoprolol and 
lisinopril. 

# Hyperlipidemia: Continued on atorvastatin.

# Obstructive sleep apnea: Continued on CPAP.
